entries.title: Psalms 77:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Night - Which to others was a time of rest and quietness.

entries.title: Psalms 77:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Troubled - Yea, the thoughts of God were now a matter of trouble, because he was angry with me. Overwhelmed - So far was I from finding relief.

entries.title: Psalms 77:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The days - The mighty works of God in former times.

entries.title: Psalms 77:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: My song - The mercies of God vouchsafed to me, and to his people, which have obliged me to sing his praises, not only in the day, but also by night.

entries.title: Psalms 77:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I said - These suspicions of God's faithfulness proceed from the weakness of my faith. The years - The years wherein God hath done great and glorious works, which are often ascribed to God's right - hand.

entries.title: Psalms 77:13
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In holiness - God is holy and just, and true in all his works.

entries.title: Psalms 77:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Afraid - And stood still, as men astonished, do.

entries.title: Psalms 77:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Poured - When the Israelites passed over the sea. Arrows - Hail - stones or lightnings.

entries.title: Psalms 77:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Not known - Because the water returned and covered them.

entries.title: Psalms 77:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Leddest - First through the sea, and afterwards through the wilderness, with singular care and tenderness, as a shepherd doth his sheep.
